mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for two consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains >2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant negative relationship with FEDFUNDS change (p > 0.05) in the identified regime, or the rate remains below 2% throughout the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) coinciding with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by >0.2% while PAYEMS increases by >5% in the same month
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the correlation between PAYEMS change and UNRATE change is not statistically significant (p > 0.05), or 20-day forward returns are not higher than baseline when the trigger occurs.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 2% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating supply-side demand, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: Three consecutive months of >2% INDPRO growth are followed by negative or flat 5-day forward returns, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for two consecutive months suggests the Fed is less likely to raise rates, reducing discount rate expectations and generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not fall below 2% in the observed window, or 20-day forward returns are not positive when the trigger is met.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly ratio of RSAFS to GDPC1 exceeds 0.8 for two consecutive months, it indicates a shift toward credit-driven demand that supports equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio rises above 0.8 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: The RSAFS/GDPC1 ratio does not exceed 0.8 in the relevant regime, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when the ratio crosses the threshold.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% followed by a decline in labor force participation (HOUST) suggests a tightening labor market, which can trigger equity market overvaluation and produce negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4% and HOUST decreases in the same month
failure_condition: In the identified regime, the combination of UNRATE <4% and HOUST decline is not associated with negative 20-day forward returns (p > 0.05), or the effect is mechanically neutral.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 3% for four consecutive months indicates deflationary pressure that reduces growth expectations and results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL does not decline for four consecutive months, or 5-day forward returns are not negative when CPIAUCSL is low.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS to above 4.5% triggers a one-month lag in S&P 500 forward returns turning negative, as higher real rates discount future equity cash flows.
failure_condition: The 3-month FEDFUNDS MA never exceeds 4.5% in the current regime, or the 20-day forward return does not turn negative after the trigger.
